body.statement: For any fixed nonempty finite \(\mathfrak G\), nonempty compact boxes, exponent array, and nonempty open \(\mathcal O\subset(0,1)^p\), there are a finite rational \(\mathcal T\subset\mathcal O\), a rational \(r_{\mathrm{id}}>0\), and a valid finite rational chart-projection cover \(\mathscr C\) such that \(\Gamma_{\mathcal T}>0\), \(\kappa_{\mathcal T}>0\), \(\Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}})>0\), and \(\mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)>0\). Here \(\Gamma_{\mathcal T}=+\infty\) when \(|\mathfrak G|=1\), and \(\Lambda_{\mathcal T}=+\infty\) when its remote pair set is empty. Consequently each within-graph moment map is globally injective; this uses local chart strong monotonicity and remote separation, not the Jacobian margin alone.
body.justification: This establishes existence of a finite transform design with distinct global and local certificates.
body.gap: Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin supplies neither a finite PGF grid nor quantitative global-injectivity and Jacobian margins over compact boxes.
body.consumer: It supplies the consistency check that the reusable certificate is searching for a nonvacuous finite-input object.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a graph tuple \(\boldsymbol d\) and write
\[
 F_{\boldsymbol d}(\theta,z)
 =\bigl(G_{r,\theta_r}(z)\bigr)_{r=1}^{K}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}polynomial\text{-}pgf\text{-}regularity}\), this map and its coefficient derivative are continuous.  For a unit parameter direction \(v\), injectivity of the coefficient-to-law differential implies that the signed derivative measure is nonzero.  If its PGF were zero on the nonempty open set \(\mathcal O\), the successive one-variable power-series uniqueness argument used in (12) would make all its coefficients zero.  Therefore, for every \((\theta,v)\in\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\times\mathbb S^{d_{\boldsymbol d}-1}\), some \(z\in\mathcal O\) satisfies
\[
 D_\theta F_{\boldsymbol d}(\theta,z)v\ne0. \tag{13}
\]
Continuity makes the same point work on a neighborhood of \((\theta,v)\).  The parameter-box--unit-sphere product is compact, so finitely many such neighborhoods cover it.  Stacking the corresponding finitely many evaluations gives a Jacobian with trivial kernel for every \(\theta\).  Repeating this over the finite graph set and taking the union of the evaluation points yields a finite preliminary grid on which
\[
 \inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}}
 \sigma_{\min}(J_{\boldsymbol d}(\theta))>0
 \qquad(\boldsymbol d\in\mathfrak G), \tag{14}
\]
because the smallest singular value is continuous on each compact box.

We construct the local charts explicitly.  At any \(\theta\), (14) gives the left inverse
\[
 L_\theta=(J(\theta)^{\mathsf T}J(\theta))^{-1}J(\theta)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Choose a rational matrix \(P_\theta\) sufficiently close to \(L_\theta\).  Continuity then gives a relative open neighborhood \(U_\theta\) and \(c_\theta>0\) such that
\[
 \frac{P_\theta J(\vartheta)+J(\vartheta)^{\mathsf T}P_\theta^{\mathsf T}}2
 \succeq c_\theta I
 \qquad(\vartheta\in U_\theta). \tag{15}
\]
Choose a finite subcover \(U_1,\ldots,U_m\).  If some \(U_i\) is the whole parameter box, retain that one set and choose any positive scale small enough for the construction below.  Otherwise, to avoid importing a covering assertion without proof, put
\[
 d(x)=\max_{1\leq i\leq m}
 \operatorname{dist}\bigl(x,\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\setminus U_i\bigr),
\]
Every complement is then nonempty and relatively closed, so each displayed distance is continuous.  Every \(x\) lies in some \(U_i\), hence \(d(x)>0\); compactness gives \(\delta=\min_xd(x)>0\).  In the whole-box case choose \(\delta>0\) arbitrarily.  Partition the rational rectangle \(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\) into finitely many closed rational boxes of Euclidean diameter below \(\delta/4\), and choose a positive rational \(r_{\boldsymbol d}<\delta/(4\sqrt{d_{\boldsymbol d}})\).  For each base box \(H\), in the nontrivial-cover case select an index \(i\) for which one point of \(H\) has distance at least \(\delta\) from \(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\setminus U_i\), and in the whole-box case select its sole index.  Set
\[
 C_H=\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\cap
 \bigl(H+[-r_{\boldsymbol d},r_{\boldsymbol d}]^{d_{\boldsymbol d}}\bigr).
\]
The diameter bounds imply \(C_H\subset U_i\), so attach the rational projection \(P_i\).  The base boxes cover the parameter box.  Moreover, if \(\theta\in H\) and \(\|\theta-\theta'\|_2<r_{\boldsymbol d}\), then \(\theta,\theta'\in C_H\).  Taking a positive rational \(r_{\mathrm{id}}\) below the finite minimum of the \(r_{\boldsymbol d}\)'s gives a valid finite rational chart-projection cover for every graph.

For \(\theta,\theta'\) in a common convex chart, let \(\Delta=\theta'-\theta\).  The fundamental theorem of calculus and (15) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \langle P\{m(\theta')-m(\theta)\},\Delta\rangle
 &=\int_0^1\Delta^{\mathsf T}PJ(\theta+t\Delta)\Delta\,dt\\
 &=\int_0^1\Delta^{\mathsf T}
 \frac{PJ+J^{\mathsf T}P^{\mathsf T}}2
 \Delta\,dt\\
 &\geq c_H\|\Delta\|_2^2.
\end{aligned} \tag{16}
\]
The minimum of the finitely many positive \(c_H\)'s is positive, proving the desired local strong-monotonicity margin.

It remains to add finitely many points for global separation.  For a fixed graph, the remote set
\[
 R_{\boldsymbol d}=\{(\theta,\theta')\in
 \Theta_{\boldsymbol d}^2:\|\theta-\theta'\|_2\geq r_{\mathrm{id}}\}
\]
is compact.  By within-graph law injectivity from \(\mathrm{lem{:}polynomial\text{-}pgf\text{-}regularity}\), each pair in this set has different laws and hence differs at some PGF evaluation in \(\mathcal O\), again by power-series uniqueness.  That strict inequality persists on a neighborhood of the pair.  A finite subcover of \(R_{\boldsymbol d}\) supplies finitely many separating points.  The same argument on each compact product \(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\times\Theta_{\boldsymbol d'}\), \(\boldsymbol d\ne\boldsymbol d'\), uses the disjoint graph-law images from the regularity lemma and supplies finitely many wrong-graph separating points.  Union these with the Jacobian grid.  Appending coordinates preserves (14) and (16), after padding each projection with zero columns.  Positive definiteness of \(W\) then turns nonzero moment differences into positive squared \(W\)-distances.  Compactness and continuity give positive minima for every nonempty remote and wrong-graph comparison set.  The declared \(+\infty\) conventions cover empty sets.

All inequalities just obtained have positive uniform margins on finitely many compact sets.  Joint continuity in the finitely many evaluation points therefore permits a sufficiently small simultaneous perturbation without destroying any inequality or chart containment.  Rational points are dense in the open set \(\mathcal O\), so choose the perturbed evaluations rational and call their set \(\mathcal T\).  We have proved
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathcal T}>0,
 \qquad \kappa_{\mathcal T}>0,
 \qquad \Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}})>0,
 \qquad \mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)>0. \tag{17}
\]
For any two within-graph parameters, (16) separates them if their distance is below \(r_{\mathrm{id}}\), and the remote bound separates them otherwise.  Thus every within-graph moment map is globally injective.  This last conclusion uses the chart and remote margins, not the Jacobian margin alone.
